analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation-only: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines 559-574 KV re-slice floors, plus a date bump) and docs/architecture/inference.md (re-slice floors, cluster health-file separation, cluster runtime facts and pair-serving grants, assistant depth-two to depth-three, and the rule that the speculative assistant serves local clusters only). No executable code changed, so I found no direct regression against the threat model.

Security-relevant claims the next pass should check against code, which is outside the supplied evidence:
1. inference.md 5254-5288 describes the coordinator holding pair members without a pair-serving grant to single-Mac requirements. It also says an undeclared model's grant covers only the modes its runtime serves today. This touches the TB-002 / TB-011 coordinator authorization contract, which is platform-owned. The cited platform commits could not be verified here.
2. The documented rule that a setup saved for coordinator pairing carries no speculative assistant (`ClusterConfiguration.validate`) is a control that the docs claim but I could not verify. Verify that it is enforced, because the verify windows have no parity qualification.
3. The separate health files (`service-health.json` and `part-health.json`) only affect liveness and watchdog behavior. They are relevant to availability under T-043 and T-057 if the guard is implemented incorrectly.
4. The re-slice floors change per-slot KV allocation (A-018, T-029). The documentation itself notes that a newcomer's floor is checked only after its engine is assembled, which can cause `no_kv_headroom`. That is an availability limitation, not a regression.

None of the changed text weakens the prefix-cache T-041 posture or the key custody and attestation assumptions. needs_deeper_review is true only because the source code behind these documented controls was not supplied.
